full_judgment:
2. In these Rules Nisi issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 6-3-2013 (Annexure-D) passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Jessore in Artha Rin Suit No. 35 of 2011 as well as the judgment and decree dated 6-3-201 (Annexure-D) passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Jessore in Artha Rin Suit No. 36 of 2011 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and hence, are of no legal effect. 

 3. In view of the statements so have been made in both the writ petitions Mr Sifar Mustafa, the learned Advocate appearing for the respective petitioners of both the writ petitions drawing attention to the impugned judgment and decree dated 6-3-20013 (Annexure-D) submits that the same has been decreed under section 13(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (in short, the Ain, 2003). In this regard, drawing attention to the said provision of law he goes to submit that in order to invoke section 13(3) the Adalat has to be satisfied that the defendants concerned have admitted the claim of the plaintiff bank and that to that effect the bank has to make an application. In this regard, referring to paragraph Nos. 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13 of the written statements so have been filed by the respective defendants including the petitioner he goes to argue that this petitioners, the defendant No. 2 has categorically denied the claim of the plaintiff bank, as is apparent therefrom; rather making an application on 24-1-2013 (Annexure-C) this petitioner brought attention to the Adalat about the disputes so have been agitated therein and made a prayer to fix up another date for peremptory hearing upon taking evidence on the assertion so made by the petitioner. But the Adalat without giving any observation and findings whatsoever on the application dated 24-1-2013 and also in the absence of any application of the respondent bank has decreed the suit invoking the provision as contained in section 13(3) of the Ain, 2003. Accordingly, he submits that both the impugned judgment and decree should be knocked down for having been passed without jurisdiction. In support he has referred the case of Md Afran Uddin Akand vs Artha Rin Adalat and others reported in 15 BLT 343. 

 4. Conversely, Mr Kazi Akhtar Hossain, the learned Advocate by filling affidavit in opposition on behalf of respondent-bank submits drawing attention to the statement so made in paragraph 13 of the written statements so filed by the defendants submits that there the petitioner has admitted the claim of the bank stating, inter-alia, "অত্র বিবাদী ইচ্ছাকৃতভাবে লোন পরিশোধ করিতে গড়িমসি করেন নাই। I" In view of the stated admissions of the defendant petitioner the Adalat has rightly exercised power under section 13(3) of the Ain in decreeing the suit. In support, he has referred the case Md Kamal Uddin Akand vs Artha Rin Adalat and other reported in VI ADC (2009) 383. He further submits that for challenging the judgment and decree this petitioner has alternative forum as provided under section 41 of the Ain, 2003. Having not invoked the same these Rules must fail on the count of maintainability 

 7. In view of the above, it is apparent that in order to pass judgment and decree under the said provision the Adalat has to be satisfied that there is an admission by the defendant concern over the claim so made by the plaintiff bank and to that effect the Bank is required to make an application. Moreso, the legislature having used the word এবং after the words “বাদীর আরজির বক্তব্য স্বীকৃত হইয়া থাকিলে” and “উক্তরুপ স্বীকৃতির ভিত্তিতে যেরুপ রায় বা আদেশ পাইতে বাদী অধিকারী” made those two requirements conjunctive. In the instant case, the defendants including the petitioner in their written statements, so filed in both the suits, have categorically disputed the claim of the plaintiff bank, as is apparent in particular from paragraph Nos. 5 and 7 of the written statements. However, on examining the entire order sheets, as have been annexed as Annexure-C-1, it does not reflect that on the alleged admission of the defendant-petitioner the bank has made an application to the Adalat with a prayer to pass judgment and decree under section 13(3) of the Ain. Rather, the Adalat has decreed the suit invoking the said provision of law and based its findings on the assertion – 

 8. This statement was not the only pleadings of the defendants, rather in their written statements they have categorically disputed the claim of the plaintiff bank and to that effect the petitioner made a prayer before the Adalat by filing an application on 24-1-2013 to fix up another date for peremptory hearing of the suit upon recording evidence on that score. But the Adalat has rejected the same and ultimately, decreed the suit under section 13(3) of the Ain without taking any evidence whatsoever. 

 9. Be that as it may, we have no manner of doubt to find that the impugned judgment and decree dated 6-3-2013 passed in connection with Artha Rin Suit Nos.35 and 36 both of 2011 have been passed without jurisdiction. The said view of ours also finds support in the case reported in 15 BLT 343 at paragraph 13 which are quoted hereinbelow— 

 12. The impugned judgment and decree dated 6-3-2013 (Annexure-D) passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 1st Court, Jessore in Artha Rin Suit Nos. 35 and 36 both of 2011 are hereby declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and hence, are of no legal effect.
